One of the League.name: One of the League
One of the League.description:
🖐️ You've been League since Hosu. Tonight Shigaraki has called everyone in, and the bar has never been this full.

📍 League Hideout Bar, Kamino Ward · Friday, July 26, early evening
🎭 Already accepted: a seat in the booth, a name they use, a cut of the pay
👥 For League of Villains Recruits
One of the League.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Friday, July 26, early evening, days before U.A. Academy's Hero Course leaves for its summer training camp. The PC is a member of the League of Villains, accepted weeks ago, not a hire on trial. Much of the year is already behind them: the League's attack on the USJ failed in April; the Sports Festival made Katsuki Bakugo famous as the winner chained snarling to the podium; at Hosu in May, Stain, the Hero Killer, was captured, and his televised stand made the League famous by association. In the days after Hosu the broker Giran brought Himiko Toga and Dabi to the door, and the PC came in at the same time, through Giran, a broker or a reason of their own from the Background (a Quirk someone saw, a grudge, a debt, a request); if the Background is silent, Giran vouched for them. Through June and July Spinner, Mr. Compress, Magne and Twice signed on too. Since then the PC has done League work: scouting, gear runs through Giran, testing a would-be recruit, a job that paid in cash. Tomura Shigaraki counts the PC as a party member and uses their name; Kurogiri pays their cut and opens gates for them.
THE PLACE: The Corner Booth of the League Hideout Bar, a cracked red leather booth at the back of the bar's one low-lit room, a few steps from the Bar Counter. Spinner's Stain clippings are taped to the wall above it.
THE MOMENT: Kurogiri messaged every member this afternoon: tonight, everyone, no excuses. (The job Tomura will name is set for the evening of Saturday, August 3.) The PC sits in the booth with the other members. Tomura Shigaraki is on his end stool at the counter with a handheld game, scratching at his neck; Kurogiri polishes glasses behind the counter and has set a rolled-up paper map beside the till. Open on the crowded room and the waiting: Toga swinging her legs, Twice arguing with himself, Dabi bored by the wall, Spinner and Magne bickering, Mr. Compress rolling a marble across his knuckles. Kurogiri says three more, people Sensei provided, come through his gate the moment Tomura starts (no set hour). End before anyone explains the map, without writing the PC's words.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Tomura Shigaraki: the leader; treats the members as his party, rates them in game terms, sulks at backtalk, and wants them at planning nights.
- Kurogiri: formal and courteous, calls him "Tomura Shigaraki", pays, opens gates, keeps the backer's secrets.
- Himiko Toga: bright, cheerful and unsettling; talks about love and blood and the people she wants to be.
- Dabi: burn-scarred, dry and bored; says little about himself and nothing about his past.
- Twice: argues with his own second voice in the same breath; loyal and afraid of coming apart. His real name is Jin Bubaigawara, but he is one person and his Character line is always "Twice".
- Spinner: a lizard-faced heteromorph who joined for Stain's ideals and wants the League to deserve them. His real name is Shuichi Iguchi, but his Character line is always "Spinner".
- Mr. Compress: a masked showman with a magician's manners.
- Magne: big-hearted and protective of the younger members, a big magnet-hammer at her side.
- Mustard, Muscular and Moonfish: the three newcomers who arrive through Kurogiri's gate later tonight; strangers to the PC.
- The monitor: now and then a calm voice Tomura calls Sensei speaks from it; it never shows a face.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Criminal Ties: Giran texts the PC during the wait: he wants a word about the gear bill after the meeting.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: Spinner slides the PC a new clipping about a heteromorph beaten in Hosu and asks what Stain would do.
- Mutant: Toga leans across the booth and asks whether the PC's blood looks as interesting as the rest of them.
- Emitter: Twice asks the PC to show the newcomers what their Quirk can do, then argues it's a terrible idea.
- Default: Toga has saved the PC a seat and wants to know where they were all week.
RULES:
- The PC is a full member: the others know their name, face and Quirk as far as the PC has used it with them, and talk freely in front of them. Their past before the League stays theirs.
- The opening stays in the bar's one room; the briefing itself is the side event "The Vanguard Action Squad", which starts on its own.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here; Sensei's plans reach the PC only through what Tomura chooses to say.
- Tomura's five-finger touch kills, so the members keep their hands off him.
THE DAYS AHEAD (background for later turns):
- Members come and go between jobs; most keep their own rooms and the bar is where they meet, drink and plan.
- League work grows with the League: scouting heroes and patrol routes, gear and papers through Giran, new recruits to test, funding jobs, covering for each other with police and pros, and roles in the League's operations.
- Until August 3 the League prepares the raid, and members get real pieces of it: scouting the mountain roads to the camp, fitting gear, gate drills with Kurogiri, sizing up and keeping the three newcomers in line, a cash job to pay for it all. Tomura hands these out as quests for his party; nobody is told to wait.
One of the League.firstQuest: Take a place in the League's first big operation: learn the job Tomura is about to name, choose your role in it, and decide what you want the League to become.
One of the League.questGenerationGuidance: Favor work inside the League as a member, varied and growing: scouting a target or a hero's patrol, buying gear and papers through Giran, testing a would-be recruit, settling a quarrel between members, a cash job to fund an operation, keeping the three newcomers in line. Members trust the PC with real pieces of the plan; never repeat the same errand. Heroes and police are dangerous and close; every job has a cost if it goes wrong.
